content.title: Fran Drescher Reacts to Her Marty Supreme Son Timothée Chalamet's Controversy: 'He'll Be More Careful Next Time' (Exclusive)
content.text: Fran Drescher; Timothee Chalamet. Credit : Jerod Harris/Getty; Gilbert Flores/Penske Media via Getty NEED TO KNOW Fran Drescher hopes Timothée Chalamet has learned from the backlash to his controversial claim that "no one cares" about the ballet or opera"I don't think that it's gonna have a lasting impact on his career — which is sensational. But, he'll be more careful next time," she tells PEOPLE in an exclusive interviewOrganizations like the Metropolitan Opera have referenced Chalamet's comments in viral TikToks and responses in the days since the comments gained attention Fran Drescher hopes Timothée Chalamet has learned from the backlash to his controversial claim that "no one cares" about the ballet or opera. The 68-year-old actress commented on Chalamet's recent comments while speaking with Danny Pellegrino, who hosted PEOPLE's exclusive coverage of the Elton John AIDS Foundation's 34th Academy Awards Viewing Party."You live, you learn," she says. "You gotta be careful what you say to the press because you could paint yourself into a corner you can't get out of. I don't think that it's gonna have a lasting impact on his career – which is sensational. But, he'll be more careful next time." Fran Drescher attends Elton John AIDS Foundation's 34th Annual Academy Awards Viewing Party on March 15, 2026 in West Hollywood, Calif. Tommaso Boddi/WireImage Drescher, who plays Chalamet's mom in Marty Supreme, continues, "Maybe he'll do less press and just be more aware of what he's saying instead of [being] so relaxed because now he sees that you could be on top and then people could turn against you. So, you gotta always be very careful." The star of The Nanny also shares her personal experience with the 30-year-old actor, saying, "I find him to be a very kind and caring person that was raised by artists." "I think that even though he may have come across a bit cavalier. In reality, I think that he has a great respect and regard for the arts," she concludes. Chalamet attended the 2026 Oscars, where he was nominated both for producing and starring in Marty Supreme. His comments were brought up several times during the broadcast, including by host Conan O'Brien in the opening monologue. "Security is extremely tight tonight," the comedian said at the start of the show. "Just got to mention that, yeah, I’m told there’s concerns about attacks from both the opera and ballet communities." Chalamet's other costar Kevin O'Leary commented on the backlash while speaking to Variety on the red carpet at the Oscars, saying, “That kid is great kid. He took a bum rap on that. By the way, he gave a lot of promo to opera houses and ballet." Timothée Chalamet at the 2026 Oscars. Getty Images Chalamet's controversial remarks about opera and ballet came during his Variety and CNN town hall on Feb. 24 with Matthew McConaughey at the University of Texas. "I admire people, and I've done it myself, who go on a talk show and say, 'Hey, we've got to keep movie theaters alive, we've gotta keep this genre alive,' and another part of me feels like if people want to see it, like Barbie, like Oppenheimer, they're going to go see it and go out of their way to be loud and proud about it," he said at the time. Related Stories "I don't want to be working in ballet, or opera, or things where it's like, 'Hey, keep this thing alive, even though like no one cares about this anymore.' All respect to all the ballet and opera people out there," he continued. Chalamet immediately recognized that his comments could be seen as disparaging, adding, "I just lost 14 cents in viewership. I just took shots for no reason." A number of professional singers and performing artists have publicly criticized Chalamet's comments in the days since the talk aired. On March 5, the New York City-based Metropolitan Opera even put out a TikTok video showcasing the work put into opera productions, which has been viewed more than 1.7 million times since it was published. "This one’s for you, Timothée Chalamet… 👀," the organization wrote in a caption to its TikTok post. See PEOPLE's coverage of the 98th Academy Awards, airing live on ABC and Hulu on March 15.
